to: AS EXECUTED: S4 $30/day to $15/day only. S2 deliberately LEFT at $25/day (month tracking under budget; the entry's own below-$6,600 over-correction rule). Account set budgets $235/day, not the $220/day originally planned. See 2026-08-27 amendment.

hypothesis: August is projecting ~$7,428 against Ben's $7,000 ceiling — the pre-registered ceiling guardrail fires. Trimming the two weakest campaigns lands the month at ~$6,950 without touching S3 (whose exposure-based probe needs its budget held to 8/24) and without touching S5 or Brand (the two producers). Expected: total spend falls ~$30/day of set budget; lead volume falls by less than proportionally, because S2 and S4 are the account's least productive dollars.

snapshot.window: 2026-08-03..2026-08-15 (August month-to-date; Aug 1-2 were a dark weekend)
snapshot.conversion_action_set: n/a — this is a spend-pacing correction, not a conversion judgement
snapshot.data_source: admin Lead Pulse weekly spend (Ads API): Aug 3 week $1,746 + Aug 10 week-to-date $1,791
snapshot.settlement_status: spend settles same-day; no restatement risk on cost
snapshot.notes: Run rate $353.70/serving day over 21 August serving days → projection $7,428, ~$428 over ceiling. Root cause is NOT the 8/12 S3 raise: Aug 3-7 ran $349/day and Aug 10-14 ran $358/day, i.e. essentially flat across the raise. The real error is the weekday-overdelivery assumption — declared 1.3x, actual 1.41x. Remaining allowance $3,463 over 11 serving days = $315/serving day → set budgets ~$223/day. S2 -$15 and S4 -$15 gives $220/day → projected ~$6,950. Monday 8/17 is a PARTIAL-effect day (edit lands ~8:30 AM after serving begins), so the first clean day at the new budgets is Tue 8/18; the projection above treats 8/17 as roughly half-effect.

review_gates.note: Pacing correction, not an economic probe. The gate is enough serving days to re-measure the run rate, not exposure to conversions.

decision_rule.prose: At the 8/24 pacing re-check, recompute the month-end projection on the post-trim run rate. Land $6,800-$7,000: hold. Above $7,000: trim again, next lever S2 to pause (see S2 diagnosis — it buys generic queries at ~4x S3's price). Below $6,600: we over-corrected and are wasting approved envelope — restore S4 first, never S2.

guardrails.s3_budget_untouched: S3 stays at $75 through the 8/24 exposure gate — protecting the probe is why this lever was chosen
guardrails.s5_and_brand_untouched: the two producers are not funded down for pacing
guardrails.lead_volume: blended weekly leads must not fall more than proportionally to the spend reduction; if they do, the cut hit productive traffic and reverses

confounders: intervention:s3-budget-raise-20260812 — this changes account composition inside S3's evaluation window; S3's own budget is untouched but account-level spend mix changes. Recorded as a reconsideration review on that entry.

S2's cut is simultaneously a pacing lever and a response to the S2 diagnosis (generic close-variant cannibalization) — the two motives are entangled and this entry must not later be read as clean evidence for either.

amendments.what: The ceiling pre-commitment (registered 8/13) named S3 as the designated lever if the August projection exceeded $7,000. Firing it as written would have ended the S3 probe four serving days into an eight-day exposure gate. Designated lever changed to S2 + S4, which are defensible on merit independently of pacing.
